commit.message:
walletrpc: reject retired lease requests

Reject retired confirmation-count protobuf fields before lease
acquisition or PSBT funding so older clients cannot silently create
timed leases. Use preserved unknown fields and the existing protobuf
wire parser to keep the retired fields out of the public request schema.

Cover both public handlers with decoded old requests and stable error
identity assertions. Keep the existing wallet lifetime implementation.

commit.message:
walletrpc: support leases without expiry

Select the existing depth-one wallet lifetime through explicit flags.
Reuse capability resolution, caller ownership and acquisition rollback,
and report the effective policy through boolean acknowledgements.

Give conflicting lifetimes and invalid owner IDs stable error
identities. Cover acquisition, validation and same-owner renewal through
the public handlers. Remove count response assignments and the obsolete
count-based RPC integration test before retiring their generated
declarations.

commit.message: docs: add release notes for #11440

lnwallet: reject a zero CSV delay

In this commit, we reject a CSV delay of zero during constraint
verification.

The CSV delay is the time the owner of a commitment must wait before
sweeping their own output, and it is the window the other party has to
respond to a breach. A delay of zero removes that window entirely and
is never a sensible value, but VerifyConstraints only bounded the delay
from above.

VerifyConstraints is the one place every delay passes through:
CommitConstraints calls it for the delay the remote party requires of
us, in both the initiator and responder roles, and the funding manager
calls it for the delay we require of the remote party. Checking for zero
there covers every channel type and both directions.

discovery: limit zombie marking to channel-level failures

In this commit, we narrow the set of on-chain validation failures that
mark a channel edge as a zombie.

A zombie entry is keyed only by the short channel ID, so it should
record a fact about the channel at that SCID: either the funding
transaction doesn't exist, or its output has been spent. A funding
script mismatch is different. It means the bitcoin keys in that one
announcement don't commit to the confirmed output, which says nothing
about the channel itself. We now reject such an announcement without
writing a zombie entry.

Invalid announcements still add a peer-scoped reject cache entry and
raise the sender's ban score, and the missing transaction and spent
output cases keep their existing zombie behavior.

The on-chain rejection test now distinguishes the three cases, and its
invalid-output fixture uses a real output built from different bitcoin
keys so that it reaches the script mismatch path.

lnwallet+chanstate: keep persisted HTLC data readable

In this commit, we tighten two invariants around the HTLC data we write
to disk.

First, we only attach aux signatures to an HTLC on taproot overlay
channels. The aux signer is configured node wide, so it also sees the
commit_sig of plain channels. Those channels never use aux signatures,
and the count check further down is already gated on the tapscript root
bit, but the attach step wasn't: any aux data unpacked for a plain
channel was copied into the HTLC's custom records and persisted with the
commitment.

Second, SerializeHtlcs now refuses to write an HTLC whose onion and extra
data exceed what ReadElement accepts for a variable length byte slice.
Before, the writer had no bound while the reader capped the field at
66,000 bytes, so an oversized HTLC was written without error but made
the whole channel unreadable on the next load. The reader's limit is now
a named constant that the writer checks against.

chainntnfs: adjust spend and dispatch log levels

In this commit, we lower the level of a few notifier log lines.

A spend that carries no witness is reported to the caller as
ErrEmptyWitnessStack, and every backend logs that error and continues.
Logging it at the critical level as well shuts the whole daemon down,
which is far out of proportion: a spend notification can legitimately
match a transaction without witness data, for example a legacy output
watched through the chain notifier RPC. We now log it as an error and
leave the handling to the caller.

We also move the per-request "skipped dispatch" messages from debug to
trace, as they fire for every already-dispatched request on each block
and add little at the debug level.

chancloser: preserve cooperative close variants

In this commit, we carry the selected closing-signature variant through the cooperative close state machine instead of reducing it to a single no-closee flag.

When a peer selects the closee-only transaction, we now omit the remote output while building and completing the local proposal, then reply with the matching signature field. This keeps both peers on the same transaction for legacy and taproot channels.
